title: An @export_file reference to a resource is not taken into account when deleting the resource
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5.stable.official [876b29033]



### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon (TM) R7 360 Series (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.20913.2000) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700 CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads) - 7.95 GiB memory

### Issue description

Referencing a resource via `@export_file` allows to have the path managed by the editor, for the purpose of moving the referenced resource to different locations within the project. But when attempting to delete the referenced resource this reference is not listed among the "Dependencies of files to be deleted", which is:
1. Different from how a direct reference works
2. Creates false impression that the resource is unreferenced

It is expected that every form of reference recognized by the editor is managed to the same extent and is accounted for by all relevant mechanisms.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a scene and a resource.
2. Add script to the scene and to it an `@export_file()` variable.
3. In the scene editor configure the variable to point to the resource, save the scene.
4. Attempt to delete the referenced resource in FileSystem view. Note how the reference is not listed in the "Please Confirm..." dialog.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[export-file-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22950522/export-file-mrp.zip)
